subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which piece of apparatus is used to add an accurately measured, variable volume of solution during a titration?
questions.explain: A burette delivers precise, variable volumes of solution and its scale is read to the nearest 0.05 cm3 in titrations.

questions.q: Which instrument is used to measure the temperature change during a reaction?
questions.explain: A thermometer measures temperature, allowing temperature changes in energy-change experiments to be recorded.

questions.q: What name is given to the variable that the experimenter deliberately changes?
questions.explain: The independent variable is the one deliberately changed to see its effect on the outcome.

questions.q: What name is given to the variable that is measured as the outcome of an investigation?
questions.explain: The dependent variable is the quantity measured, which depends on changes made to the independent variable.

questions.q: Why must control variables be kept the same throughout an investigation?
options: To make it a fair test so results are valid
To make the reaction happen faster
To increase the number of anomalies
questions.explain: Keeping control variables constant ensures only the independent variable affects the result, making the test fair and the results valid.

questions.q: Which technique is used to separate an insoluble solid from a liquid?
questions.explain: Filtration through filter paper traps the insoluble solid (residue) while the liquid (filtrate) passes through.

questions.q: Which technique would you use to obtain pure water from a sample of salt solution?
questions.explain: Simple distillation evaporates then condenses the water, leaving the dissolved salt behind to give pure water.

questions.q: Paper chromatography is used to separate and identify which type of mixture?
options: Mixtures of soluble, coloured substances such as dyes
Two liquids with very different boiling points
questions.explain: Chromatography separates soluble substances such as dyes because each travels a different distance up the paper.

questions.q: How is the Rf value of a spot in paper chromatography calculated?
options: Distance moved by the substance divided by distance moved by the solvent front
Distance moved by the solvent front divided by distance moved by the substance
Distance moved by the substance multiplied by distance moved by the solvent front
Distance moved by the substance added to distance moved by the solvent front
questions.explain: Rf = distance moved by substance / distance moved by solvent front, always giving a value between 0 and 1.

questions.q: In a chromatogram a spot moves 4 cm while the solvent front moves 8 cm. What is the Rf value of the spot?
questions.explain: Rf = 4 cm / 8 cm = 0.5.

questions.q: What is an anomalous result?
options: A result that does not fit the pattern of the other results
The mean of all the results
The most precise result in the set
A result that is repeated three times
questions.explain: An anomalous result stands out from the trend of the other data and is usually caused by an error.

questions.q: What should you do with an anomalous result before calculating a mean?
options: Ignore it and exclude it from the mean
Use it as the final answer
Add it to every other result
questions.explain: Anomalies are excluded from the mean so they do not distort the calculated average.

questions.q: Why should eye protection (safety goggles) be worn during many chemistry experiments?
options: To protect the eyes from chemical splashes
To keep the reaction at constant temperature
questions.explain: Goggles protect the eyes from splashes of corrosive or irritant chemicals, reducing the risk of injury.

questions.q: Which apparatus should be used to measure out exactly 25.0 cm3 of a solution into a conical flask in a titration?
questions.explain: A volumetric pipette accurately delivers a fixed volume such as 25.0 cm3, more precisely than a measuring cylinder.

questions.q: A student records these maximum temperatures: 21, 22, 23, 30 and 22 degrees C. After identifying and excluding the anomaly, what is the mean temperature?
questions.explain: The 30 degrees C reading is anomalous; the mean of 21, 22, 23 and 22 is 88/4 = 22 degrees C.

questions.q: Why is it good practice to repeat measurements and calculate a mean?
options: It improves reliability and helps identify anomalies
It removes the need for control variables
questions.explain: Repeating readings and averaging them improves reliability and makes anomalous results easier to spot.

questions.q: Which piece of apparatus is used to measure the mass of a solid reactant?
questions.explain: A balance measures mass, typically to the nearest 0.01 g for accurate quantities of solid.

questions.q: What is the key feature of a fair test?
options: Only the independent variable is changed while control variables are kept constant
Every variable is changed at the same time
The dependent variable is kept constant
questions.explain: In a fair test only the independent variable is altered, so any change in the outcome can be attributed to it.

questions.q: A student investigates how temperature affects reaction rate by timing how long a cross takes to disappear. What is the independent variable?
options: Time taken for the cross to disappear
questions.explain: Temperature is the variable deliberately changed, so it is the independent variable; the time measured is the dependent variable.

questions.q: A reaction between marble chips and acid produces carbon dioxide gas. Which apparatus is best for measuring the volume of gas released over time?
questions.explain: A gas syringe collects the gas and directly measures its volume, allowing the volume produced over time to be recorded.
